name: Mün Chin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Mün Chin (munc1235, K'cho/Mindat) is not in the catalog. this search of works with stress in the title's single title hit, Byrd 2006 'Relating prosody and dynamic events: Comments on the papers by Cho and Smiljanić' (Laboratory Phonology 8), is a Glottolog false positive: the saved Glottolog record states the language link is a 'computerized assignment from \"cho\"', and Crossref shows the 'Cho' is Taehong Cho's chapter on English lip kinematics. It is irrelevant to Mün Chin and to word stress; closed access; priority none. No first-hand word-stress statement for Mün Chin was found. The material already held by the project in the folder from our earlier reading (Nolan 2000 on tone, Nolan 2002 orthography, Mang 2006 thesis, So-Hartmann 1988, Bedell 2000/2008) was a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence and is silent (Mang 2006's only 'verb stress' line is a Turkish example from Givón). The one additional item located, Bohnert, Ziegler & Berkson 2025 JASA abstract (Crossref abstract saved), describes the inventory and four tones and says nothing about stress. sealang.net URL guesses for Nolan 2003 'Verbal alternation in K'cho' returned 404. Best remaining acquisition targets for a stress statement remain Jordan 1969 (Chin dictionary and grammar, mimeograph) and Nolan 2003 (ICSTLL36 phonological outline of verb stems), both print only. Files with updated.

sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2023. Kuki-Chin phonology: an overview. Himalayan Linguistics 22(1). doi:10.5070/H922153229
sources.note: K'Cho cited only for /kx kɣ/ onset clusters (Mang 2006:14); generic discussion of sesquisyllabic minor+major syllables in Southern KC; no K'cho-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Smith, Wendy & Noel Mann. 2009. Chin bibliography with selected annotations. Chiang Mai: Payap University Linguistics Institute. 101 pp.
sources.note: Bibliography only; used to enumerate K'cho sources (Jordan 1969 mimeograph; Nolan 2000, 2003, 2006; Bedell papers; Mang 2006). Its annotation of Nolan 2000/2006 mentions tone only.

sources.citation: Mang, Kee Shein. 2006. A syntactic and pragmatic description of verb stem alternation in K'Chò, a Chin language. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xvi+123 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Sec. 1.5.1 (pp. 14-15) gives 28 consonants, 7 vowels with length, and 'Nolan (2000) identified four tones in K'Chò: high, low, rising, and falling.. Vowel length is also contrastive'; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent and phonology section read).

sources.citation: So-Hartmann, Helga. 2009. A descriptive grammar of Daai Chin. STEDT Monograph 7. Berkeley.
sources.note: For DAAI (not K'cho): phonological word = optional unstressed presyllable + stressed main syllable, 'an IAMBIC stress contour'. Mentions Cho/Ngmüün only for classification and prior research (pp. 19-26); no stress statement for K'cho.

sources.citation: VanBik, Kenneth. 2009. Proto-Kuki-Chin: a reconstructed ancestor of the Kuki-Chin languages. STEDT Monograph 8. Berkeley.
sources.note: Mindat Cho data from Jordan 1969 and Nolan; remarks on implosives and orthography (Jordan 1969:4-5 grammar section); nothing on Mindat Cho stress.

sources.citation: Bedell, George. 2008. Agreement in K'cho. Journal of Language and Culture (Mahidol University) 27(2).
sources.note: Published version of the agreement paper (consultant from Sit Hmawi village, Mindat); no phonology or stress remarks in the pages read.

sources.citation: Nolan, Stephen. 2002. The alphabet and spelling in 'Cho. Asian Cultural Studies (International Christian University, Tokyo) 28: 127-138. doi:10.34577/00001626
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives phoneme-letter values, four tones (high unmarked, low, rising, falling), vowel length, and 'three presyllables /m/, /ng/ and the preglottal', calling the preglottal presyllable 'non-syllabic'; no statement of word stress or prominence.

sources.citation: Bedell, George. 2000. Agreement in Cho. Paper, 33rd ICSTLL, Ramkhamhaeng University, Bangkok. 14 pp.
sources.note: Morphosyntax of verb agreement only; no phonology (first three pages scanned and read).

sources.citation: Nolan, Stephen. 2000. An initial description of tone in 'Cho. Papers from the 33rd International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics, Ramkhamhaeng University, Bangkok, pp. 69-78.
sources.note: Nothing. Describes three contrastive tones (high, low, rising) plus a restricted falling tone, a high-long vs high-short vowel-length contrast, k-resyllabification, and tone sandhi on cuh/ci/lo/ni/mi; the words stress/accent do not occur (whole paper read via scanned).

sources.citation: So-Hartmann [Hartmann], Helga. 1988. Notes on the Southern Chin languages. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 11(2): 98-119.
sources.note: Comparative survey wordlists incl. Ngmüün (=Mün/K'cho); states 'Tone and/or register was not marked consistently in most of the lists, so I have not attempted to discuss it'; notes the Cho group has prenasalization/preglottalization; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bohnert, Amanda, Grayson Ziegler & Kelly H. Berkson. 2025. An initial acoustic investigation of the Mindat (K'Cho) phonetic inventory. JASA 157(4 Suppl.): A330 (ASA meeting poster) and any follow-up IU Chin Languages Research Project paper on Mindat.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.quote: Nolan (2002) also reports a seven-vowel system /i ɛ a ə ɨ o u/ with all monophthongs contrasting for length, six diphthongs /ɛj aj əj ɨ oj uj/, and four tones (high, low, rising, falling). Using data from one speaker, we provide an acoustic description of the Mindat phonetic inventory, including (but not limited to) measures of VOT for stops, center of gravity for fricatives/affricates, formant measures/trajectories for vowels, and pitch tracks for tones.
sources.locator: abstract (the item is a meeting abstract; abstract = full text)
sources.note: First acoustic documentation of K'cho; the poster/follow-up may report duration/intensity asymmetries between presyllables and main syllables.

sources.citation: Nolan, Stephen. 2021. Tone and pitch lowering behaviour in K'cho. Paper presented at the Australian Linguistic Society annual conference (La Trobe University); and any resulting La Trobe thesis/article by Nolan on K'cho prosody.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent prosodic work on K'cho by the main phonologist of the language; a prosody paper is where a stress/prominence statement would appear.
